This week we learned about microplastics with Dr. Dimitri Deheyn, a researcher at Scripps Oceanography.

🌬 Humans breathe about 10,000 liters of air a day. Along with it come 150 to 200 plastic particles.
🐋 Whale sharks filter 40,000 liters of seawater daily just to eat. Thousands of particles flow through them.
💧 More than 90% of drinking water tested contains microplastics.
👗 Ghana’s Kantamanto Market receives 15 million secondhand garments every week. About 40% become waste, overwhelming landfills and beaches. Locals call it “waste colonialism.”
🧴 Some cosmetics still contain microbeads. They’re banned in the U.S., but imports can slip through.

Minutes of use. Centuries of impact.

Big ideas. Cutting-edge research. The Social Study.

This week we learned about Nathan Harrison, San Diego’s first Black homesteader. Born enslaved in Kentucky in the 1830s, freed during the Gold Rush, and buried in an unmarked grave in Mount Hope Cemetery. He spoke Luiseno, Spanish, and English. He gifted water to travelers instead of selling it. He built alliances with both Native and settler communities. And he played into tourist expectations because it kept him alive.

That’s what The Social Study is about. Real research, surprising insights, and topics you probably didn’t cover in school.
